newsitem.title: UK: Dirty Caribbean tanker rates spike up, others quie.
newsitem.headline: Dirty Caribbean tanker rates spike up, others quie.

text.p: The western hemisphere was the liveliest sector of the dirty tanker market on Monday, with rates spiking up on a shortage of tonnage, brokers said.
Rates hit as high as W151 on 70,000 tonners Caribs/upcoast U.S., some 30 points up from last week.
One broker said around W150 was the "natural level" for this sector. "W150 is going to stay and it could go higher," he added.
He cited a lack of vessels in the Caribbean after a couple had been fixed on transatlantic routes and the drying up of oil company relets after a few had been seen on the market.

Caribs/USAC 50,000 tonne fuel oil edged up to W185/190 from around W170/175. "If you are looking in the (March) 3-5 range there are not a lot of good ships available...There's a lack of quality tonnage," another broker said.
Other sectors were little changed in typical Monday trade.
Very large crude carriers from the Middle East to Japan remained depressed at W57.5, down about 7.5 points from a week ago, with cargoes to the west and Singapore at W50.
In the West Africa/U.S. sector, million barrel rates continued soft with the Tromso Trust laden with 137,000 tonnes fixed at W89 for Sun.
Transatlantic VLCCs were flat at W65, while inter-U.K./Cont 80,000 tonners edged up to W112.5 on weather delays, brokers said.

Cross-Med 80,000 tonners showed few signs of life at W107.5/110, having slipped some five points late last week when many brokers were away from their desks for IP Week. The million-barrel Med market was also quiet.
Inter-U.K./Cont fuel oil edged down to W200 for 25,000 tonnes, while cross-Med cargoes were little changed at about W190, brokers said.
